items.title: Controlled worker dispatch
items.summary: Completed Task 111 with a separate task:dispatch permission-gated path that lets an authorized owner explicitly dispatch one pending Task through the existing Task 68 ResourceManager, Task 69 durable FIFO queue and Task 70 controlled execution cleanup. Preflight verifies the Task and any associated Project, current Agent route, configured global/provider/model slots and loopback Ollama target; route expectations are rechecked before execution. Dispatch never uses cloud Providers or Tools, automatically retries or replays work. Queued and interrupted claims require an explicit human resolution that abandons queue membership without changing Task state. The UI distinguishes actual queue/Task execution state and recorded results/errors from outcome verification. Validation: 38 focused queue, controlled-execution, local-access and dispatch API regressions passed with one existing Starlette deprecation warning; 13 Task browser-module tests and 14 public documentation tests passed; Pylance reported no problems in the nine changed Python files checked. The full Python suite reported 943 passed, 2 failed and 6 skipped. The same unrelated model-assignment tests recorded at Task 110 failed again; their tests and implementations were not changed. Tests use deterministic Provider fakes; no live or paid Provider calls were made. The default local launcher has no configured Task 68 budgets or budget setup UI, so dispatch remains unavailable until the embedding host configures explicit global/provider/model capacity. The queue UI shows at most the oldest 100 records; cross-process coordination and exactly-once execution are unsupported. Checkpoint tag: task-111-controlled-worker-dispatch. Tasks 101–111 are complete; Task 112 is next.

items.title: Chat proposals and pending Task review
items.summary: Completed Task 110 with a coordinator chat review flow that prepares a canonical, principal-scoped proposal from a completed assistant message and displays objective, responsible Agent, Project, authorized context, expected outcome, verification method, evidence and Task fields before confirmation. A distinct chat-task:create permission authorizes this flow only; local-owner mode retains no general task:create authority. Confirmation requires the exact server-generated digest, same authenticated principal, open source conversation/message, unchanged coordinator/Agent/Project/context and a 15-minute expiry. It consumes the proposal before creating one pending Task through existing persistence; no Task or Tool executes. Proposals are bounded process-local records, owner-memory context is optional and is revalidated, and durable Task descriptions keep provenance references rather than copied memory text. Validation: 36 focused Python regressions passed with one existing Starlette deprecation warning; 9 coordinator-chat browser tests and 13 public-documentation tests passed. The full Python suite reported 937 passed, 2 failed and 3 skipped; both failures are unrelated model-assignment tests that fail identically in isolation and are documented in the task evidence. Tests cover edited/stale/replayed proposals, cross-owner denial, context scope denial, duplicate creation and no provider execution on confirmation. Checkpoint tag: task-110-chat-proposals-pending-task-review. Tasks 111–128 remain planned; Task 111 is next.

items.title: Capability-based assignment policy
items.summary: Completed Task 109 with a separately enabled, disabled-by-default, principal-scoped local-owner policy for review-only Agent/model recommendations. Eligibility requires an allowed registered provider, a fresh owner-recorded inventory reference (24 hours), fully configured eligible Task 71 capacity, an explicit owner-defined budget/unit, and fresh positive tested evidence (30 days) for each Agent-declared capability. Declarations, stale/missing evidence, unknown cost, access and capacity gaps remain visible as rationale/unknowns; model names and installation are not expertise evidence. Candidate order is deterministic. The policy never changes assignments, reserves capacity, calls Providers, connects online models, transfers data, or grants cloud consent. Existing manual assignments remain authoritative; Task 108's preview/confirmation is the override path, and disabling the policy is the full undo because it never applies assignments. Inventory, capability evidence and cost estimates are caller-supplied and not independently verified; provider health, hardware feasibility, compatibility and execution readiness remain unknown. Validation: 184 directly affected Python regressions passed with no skips and one existing Starlette deprecation warning; 13 browser-module tests and 13 public-docs tests passed with deterministic fakes. Pylance reported no problems in changed Python files; no live/paid provider calls were made. Checkpoint tag: task-109-capability-based-assignment-policy. Tasks 110–128 remain planned; Task 110 is next.

items.title: Manual AI assignment and individual Employee chat
items.summary: Completed Task 108 with explicit local-model/Gemini assignment previews covering Agent identity, old/new model, privacy, assigned Tasks and owner-visible conversations; incomplete reads block mutation, stale observations conflict, and active Agent execution blocks reassignment. Task dispatch verifies its provider/model snapshot and fails rather than silently changing an existing job. Added bounded, process-local, principal-owned Employee chat with registered Employee/Agent checks, fixed provider/model/provider-instance snapshots, separate local-owner-only employee-chat permissions, conversation isolation, same-origin CSRF writes and inert rendering. Individual chats transfer only the request and recent history; Employee profiles and Task context are not attached automatically. Gemini turns retain per-turn consent, and recognized key pastes are rejected before saving or sending; the existing coordinator chat consent boundary still includes configured chat context. The one-Gemini-Agent constraint remains; disconnect/reconnect to switch. Restart loses conversations, and direct registry mutations, external processes and multiple app instances are outside assignment synchronization. Validation: 150 directly affected Python regressions, 12 browser-module tests and 13 public-docs tests passed with deterministic fakes; the Python run had one existing Starlette deprecation warning and no skips. Pylance reported no problems in changed Python files. Checkpoint tag: task-108-manual-ai-connection-assignment-individual-chat. Tasks 109–128 remain planned; Task 109 is next.

items.title: Editable corporation positions
items.summary: Completed Task 107 with an authorized /ui/positions page and protected position API backed by a bounded, per-application-service in-memory registry. Explicit local-owner mode grants distinct position:read and position:manage permissions; the default API remains fail-closed. Ten supported role templates, responsibilities, optional Employee references, reporting relationships, activation state and revision provenance are managed independently of Employee roles and Agent/model assignments. Updates reject stale revisions and reporting cycles; removal rejects records with Employee/reporting references or revision history. Position titles grant no authority, and Task/workflow records are not linked. Records are lost at restart. A position reader without employee:read still sees positions; employee choices are withheld while existing references are preserved. Validation: 45 focused Python regressions, 3 position UI tests and 13 public documentation tests passed. Tasks 108–128 remain planned; Task 108 is next.

items.title: Secure chat-driven connection onboarding
items.summary: Completed Task 106 with browser and API blocking for recognized Google AIza API-key tokens and GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY assignment pastes before any chat history persistence or provider call; the secret is cleared from the chat field and never echoed. Chat directs owners to the existing separate Gemini setup form. Online setup accepts only the standard Google AIza key shape and rejects unsupported formats before catalog/network calls. Detection is best-effort; rotating a connected key requires explicit disconnect/erase followed by rediscovery/reconnect. Existing per-turn consent, five generation attempts per key per run, 1,024 output tokens, no retries and no app-enforced dollar cap remain unchanged. Focused validation: 13 Python tests, 10 coordinator-chat/online-setup JavaScript tests and 13 public-docs tests passed. Tasks 107–128 remain planned.

items.title: First official online chat provider
items.summary: Completed Task 105 with explicit, per-turn cloud consent for Gemini coordinator chat through the existing Provider and Orchestrator. The restricted API key is held only in process memory for at most one hour; discovery uses the fixed official catalog, generation is bounded to five attempts per key per app run and 1,024 output tokens, with a 20-second timeout, bounded input/response, no retries and no fallback. A separate local-owner setup page supports model discovery, explicit assignment, staged-key erasure, status and disconnect/restore; the default API remains unchanged and fail-closed. No dollar cap is claimed; owners must set Google billing limits and alerts. Credentials are not persisted, chat permission does not imply consent, and external key use is not counted. Tasks 106–128 remain planned.

items.title: Local installed-model discovery and selection
items.summary: Completed Task 104 with explicit bounded loopback Ollama inventory through the Provider abstraction, truthful unknown/unavailable states, safe source/time evidence and a local model-setup page. Separate local-model:select authority freshly rechecks installed IDs and rejects active owned-chat requests; changed assignments require new conversations while preserving old identity/history. Selection is per-run and guarded within one service instance only; external configuration and direct paths remain unsynchronized. No download, provider switch, Task execution, slot reservation, cloud fallback or Task 105 behavior is added.

items.title: Documentation consistency and Copilot handoff audit
items.summary: Reconciled public documentation with Task 63 project-association persistence and Tasks 102-103 local login/chat boundaries. Clarified Task 101 as an initial source-review slice, historical update limitations, and the unresolved Task 104 model-selection authority gate. Preserved all Task 1-100 definitions and Tasks 104-128 planned status; runtime behavior and permissions are unchanged.

items.title: Shared post-100 task contracts
items.summary: Published Tasks 101–128 on the public documentation Tasks page, preserving all Task 1–100 foundation definitions. Tasks 101–103 carry verified checkpoint, validation and limitation records; Tasks 104–128 remain planned with dependencies, acceptance checks, exclusions and unresolved owner decision gates. Added next-task navigation and shared engineering/handoff rules so implementing AIs use one authoritative contract. This documentation change implements no future runtime capability and grants no new permissions.

items.title: Owned coordinator browser chat
items.summary: Added principal-owned coordinator chat list/create/get/send/close through application services, distinct chat permissions, generated conversation IDs, local overlapping-request rejection, bounded in-memory history and plain-text browser rendering. Explicit Send reuses CorporationChatService and Orchestrator; failed replies are recorded safely without automatic replay. Local owner mode grants scoped chat alongside reads; default API access remains rejecting. No Task/tool execution, capacity reservation, assignment mutation, streaming, true cancellation, model discovery, transcript persistence, installer or new dependencies are added.

items.title: Local owner Web UI access
items.summary: Added an explicitly configured loopback-only local launcher with hidden password prompts, expiring in-memory HttpOnly sessions, logout revocation, bounded login attempts, Host/Origin checks and session CSRF protection. Existing read permissions are available after sign-in; management and maintenance writes remain denied. The default API still rejects access without a configured authentication backend. No browser chat, provider calls, installer, remote identity integration or new dependencies are added; sessions do not survive restart.

items.title: ERSELMETZ AI CORPORATION Platform
items.summary: Added CorporationApplicationService.platform_overview() as a bounded immutable snapshot of Corporation/Node identity, existing registry counts, and the Task 92 capability catalog. Capability records preserve evidence, supplied requirements, policy boundaries, and limitations; registered, configured, unavailable, and unknown source states remain distinct. Missing ToolRegistry configuration is not reported as an empty registry, and unsupplied Gemini metadata remains UNKNOWN. The report makes no readiness or production claim, does not check Provider/model availability, assess hardware feasibility or resource capacity, or make routing decisions, and performs no Provider/network calls, Task execution, reservations, assignment changes, persistence, or API/UI work. Reads are sequential, not atomic; post-100 platform gaps remain planned.

items.title: Self-Improvement Pipeline
items.summary: Added a bounded review-only snapshot of recorded Task 95 capability workflows. It reports exact status, stage, and events; checks candidate/evaluation linkage and rechecks current workspace, approval, and checkpoint links against recorded identifiers and hashes. Test results and review evidence are marked unverifiable because source reports are not retained. The report does not invoke stages, alter workflows or assignments, create or execute Tasks, call Providers, or adopt/activate capabilities. Cross-service reads are sequential, not atomic. Task 100 remains planned.

items.title: Adaptive Workforce
items.summary: Added caller-authored immutable review proposals for Employee headcount targets by exact role and proposed changes to existing Employee roles/responsibilities, linked to Task 96 priorities with bounded rationale and source references. Current headcounts are read from the registered Employee roster (bounded to 1,000); role changes require matching current Employee snapshots to reject stale requests. Rationales and source references are not independently verified. Proposals are not generated recommendations or approvals and never alter Employee, Agent/model, Task, or Task 71 resource assignments. Targets are not reconciled with individual role changes, and Employee records are read without an atomic snapshot. Tasks 99–100 remain planned.

items.title: Organization-Level Orchestration
items.summary: Added a bounded immutable review report linking an existing Task 96 priority to a registered Employee responsibility and actual Task 85 maintenance or Task 95 capability-integration workflow records. Workflow IDs are verified in their owning services and must carry their source-specific APPROVED exact-patch decision; status, stage, hashes, approval request, and checkpoint are preserved. Caller-selected priority/responsibility fit is not inferred, Task 95 approval is not capability adoption, and the report does not change assignments, claim queue entries, schedule or execute work, call Providers, create Tasks, or persist. At Task 97 completion, Tasks 98–100 remained planned.

items.title: Corporation Planning System
items.summary: Added a bounded immutable in-memory organization plan from explicit caller-supplied priorities, constraints, rationales, and source references. Priority order is caller-defined and preserved; references are not independently verified. Planning does not inspect Projects or Tasks, rank priorities, change assignments, schedule or execute work, call Providers, or persist plans. At Task 96 completion, Tasks 97–100 remained planned.

items.title: Controlled Capability Integration
items.summary: Added a bounded caller-driven workflow record linking a Task 93 candidate and matching Task 94 report to an explicitly supplied patch workspace, matching passing Task 80/82 results, Task 81 review evidence containing the exact diff, Task 83 patch approval, and Task 84 checkpoint. The candidate/workspace link and test/review report provenance are not independently verified; approval applies only to exact patch/source hashes. The workflow invokes none of these stages and stops at CHECKPOINTED without registering or activating a capability. At Task 95 completion, Tasks 96–100 remained planned.

items.title: Capability Evaluation
items.summary: Added deterministic, bounded evidence-coverage reports for caller-supplied capability candidates across fit, risk, and operational-requirement dimensions. Caller-reported assessments and source references are preserved but not independently verified; missing dimensions remain UNKNOWN. Evaluation does not score, rank, recommend, approve, authorize, register, or activate candidates, and makes no Provider call or runtime change. At Task 94 completion, Tasks 95–100 remained planned.

items.title: Capability Discovery
items.summary: Added bounded, immutable intake of up to 100 explicitly caller-supplied capability candidates with retained source references and explicit caller-supplied provenance. Candidates are not independently verified. Discovery performs no external lookup, evaluation, ranking, registration, permission grant, activation, persistence, Provider call, or Task execution. At Task 93 completion, Tasks 94–100 remained planned.

items.title: Capability Registry
items.summary: Added a read-only, bounded capability inventory aggregated from existing Agent declarations, registered Tool metadata, non-granting IntegrationCapability scopes, and optional caller-supplied Gemini catalog snapshots. Immutable records distinguish declared, registered, scope-only, and service-reported evidence, identify source owners, retain known requirements and policy boundaries, and preserve Gemini snapshot time/count/completeness. Missing requirements remain unknown. Reads are sequential across independent registries; the registry does not call Gemini, persist/register capabilities, grant access, execute Tools/Tasks, rank/select models, or mutate assignments. At Task 92 completion, Tasks 93–100 remained planned.

items.title: External Service Integration
items.summary: Added explicit, on-demand Gemini model discovery against a fixed HTTPS endpoint using a trusted backend API-key configuration. The key is sent only in the x-goog-api-key header and is omitted from URLs, logs, errors, audit events, and result records. Responses are limited to 512 KiB each and at most five pages of 100 models, with no retries. Immutable results include only model IDs, allowlisted service-reported capability metadata, a completeness flag, and a metadata-only audit event; failures are sanitized and carry safe audit metadata. Audit events are caller-retained, not persisted automatically. No content generation, model/Agent assignment, Task execution, Provider changes, chat key entry, general credential store, API/UI, or background polling is added. Tasks 92–100 remain planned.

items.title: Computer-Use Capability
items.summary: Added caller-driven, read-only browser inspection that reuses Task 88's exact-host HTTPS allowlist and bounded fetch. Scripts, styles, resource URLs, event attributes, and active embedded content are removed before static markup is rendered in an ephemeral headless Chromium context; JavaScript, downloads, user interaction, local-file access, and browser network requests are unavailable. Immutable results are bounded untrusted evidence with user-visible safeguards. No API/UI, persistence, Agent/Provider calls, Task execution, or background polling is added. Tasks 91–100 remain planned.

items.title: Coding Tool Integration
items.summary: Added an opt-in MCP coding-tool proposal adapter over explicitly registered MCPTool instances. Callers supply a bounded instruction and selected path/content pairs; the tool returns a bounded unified diff limited to those paths. The result includes source/patch digests and is not applied, executed, persisted, tested, or reviewed automatically. Task 79 and Task 80/81 remain separate caller actions. MCP servers remain trusted host processes, not OS sandboxes. Tasks 90–100 remain planned.

items.title: Browser/Web Research Capability
items.summary: Added explicit HTTPS page retrieval through an immutable exact-host allowlist that defaults to empty. Redirects and environment proxies are disabled; requests have a 10-second timeout, a 512 KiB response limit, and a 20,000-character extracted-text limit. HTML/plain-text results are immutable and classified as untrusted evidence; instruction-like retrieved text is never executed or sent to an Agent/Provider. No search, crawling, API/UI, persistence, Task execution, or background polling is added. At Task 88 completion, Tasks 89–100 remained planned.

items.title: GitHub Integration
items.summary: Added authenticated, read-only public GitHub repository inspection requiring github:read and an explicit immutable repository allowlist. The default scope is empty; out-of-scope, missing, and private repositories share a not-found response, and out-of-scope requests make no GitHub call. The response omits README text. No credentials, private-repository access, branch/commit/pull-request writes, Task execution, Agent calls, or separate approval records are added; permission plus repository scope are the agreed gates. At Task 87 completion, Tasks 88–100 remained planned.

items.title: MCP Integration
items.summary: Added an opt-in synchronous MCP client for explicitly selected local stdio or in-process tools. A frozen tool allowlist, explicit ToolRegistry registration, bounded JSON inputs and text/structured results, per-call timeouts, and sanitized errors keep the adapter scoped. It does not connect tools to Agents, Tasks, APIs, or UI, or perform background discovery/polling. Custom process environments are rejected; local MCP servers are trusted host processes, not OS sandboxes. At Task 86 completion, Tasks 87–100 remained planned.

items.title: Controlled Self-Maintenance
items.summary: Added a bounded caller-driven workflow record linking an existing failed Task to its diagnostic, proposal, patch workspace, one Task 80 or Task 82 test result, and Task 81 review of evidence containing the exact patch. Only a PASSED test and recorded review make it ready for Task 83 approval; review findings remain advisory. Task 83 decisions and Task 84 checkpoints are separately invoked and recorded only after workspace/hash linkage checks. Snapshots are in-memory (up to 100 workflows); metadata-only audit events use existing Task logs. A failed test ends that workflow. No hidden Provider/test/approval/checkpoint calls, automatic retries, background work, Task creation/execution, patch application, API/UI, or assignment/resource changes are added; at Task 85 completion, Tasks 86–100 remained planned.

items.title: Git Checkpoint Integration
items.summary: Added an authenticated local checkpoint API requiring maintenance:checkpoint in addition to exact Task 83 approval. It revalidates the registered Task 79 patch/source, requires a clean Git worktree and index, and atomically records the approved diff as a commit on a dedicated local branch using a temporary index; it does not switch branches, push, merge, run Tasks, or alter the active checkout. Checkpoint creator identity is recorded. Branches/commits persist locally; reports are in-memory, and recovery after later integration is an explicit git revert.

items.title: Human Approval Workflow
items.summary: Added an authenticated in-memory maintenance review workflow that presents the exact unified diff and binds approval/rejection to the registered workspace plus patch/source SHA-256 hashes. API decisions require maintenance:approve, echo both hashes, record the authenticated reviewer identity and UTC time, and reject stale or disposed workspaces; the configured backend must grant approval permission only to human reviewers. Approval checks fail closed for future consumers. Task 83 itself applies no patch, performs no Git operation, and executes no Task; Task 84 separately implements local checkpoints.

items.title: Maintenance Sandbox
items.summary: Added a separate Docker-only test path for registered Task 79 workspaces, transferring bounded selected files into an ephemeral no-network/no-host-mount container with resource/runtime/output limits and automatic removal. Requires an explicitly approved, locally present immutable image; missing Docker or controls block without host fallback. Task 80's existing host-permission test workflow remains unchanged, and the Docker daemon/image remain trusted prerequisites.

items.title: Automated Code Review
items.summary: Added a one-call, caller-selected Agent review over bounded caller-supplied sanitized evidence, with severity/area classifications and citations restricted to supplied references. Evidence is sent to the selected Agent's configured Provider; callers authorize disclosure. Results are advisory; no files, workspaces, Tasks, tests, assignments, proposals, approvals, or Git state are accessed or changed.

items.title: Automated Testing Workflow
items.summary: Added caller-selected Python pytest execution against a separate temporary copy of a registered Task 79 workspace, with no shell, dependency installation, a 120-second process timeout, 64 KiB output cap, reduced environment, and immutable reports of actual status/output. Test code still runs with host permissions; this is not an OS sandbox.

items.title: Automated Patch Development
items.summary: Added bounded application of caller-supplied unified diffs to explicitly selected existing files in a disposable temporary copy; source files remain unchanged, and no code, tests, Providers, Tasks, assignments, or Git operations are invoked. The temporary copy is not a security sandbox; approval and checkpoint workflows remain separate tasks.

items.title: Maintenance Proposals
items.summary: Added immutable in-memory caller-authored maintenance proposals linked to Task 77 diagnostics, with bounded explicit change, scope, and risk fields; proposals are review-only and do not generate patches, persist, execute Tasks, modify assignments, or apply changes.

items.title: Diagnostic Agent
items.summary: Added one-call, caller-selected Agent diagnostics over bounded caller-supplied evidence only, with validated bounded summaries and citations restricted to supplied reference IDs; no automatic retrieval, raw error input, Task creation/execution, assignment changes, retries, or remediation.

items.title: Error Detection
items.summary: Added persisted routing- and execution-stage failure categories, migrated historical failed Tasks to UNKNOWN, and exposed bounded immutable failure summaries with Task IDs and category codes only; raw exception text, retries, Task execution, and lifecycle changes are excluded.

items.title: System Monitoring
items.summary: Added an on-demand immutable report over local Task status, Provider registration, and configured resource-capacity snapshots, with bounded factual failure and exhausted-capacity signals; Provider availability remains UNKNOWN, and monitoring performs no probes, polling, persistence, Task execution, or runtime changes.

items.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.summary: Added bounded caller-driven in-memory handoffs among 2–10 distinct registered Agents on an existing pending Task, with registered-role verification, append-only shared context, explicit terminal failure/completion, and metadata-only Task audit events; no Provider calls, Task lifecycle changes, assignment changes, Task creation, or API/UI.

items.title: Intelligent Model Routing
items.summary: Added bounded review-only model candidate selection from explicit caller-supplied capability, policy-tag, provider-availability, and cost-estimate metadata; selection preserves candidate order, excludes UNKNOWN availability unless opted in, reports Task 71 admission separately, and never changes assignments or executes Tasks.

items.title: Provider Availability
items.summary: Added optional synchronous provider availability checks with immutable AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN results, a safe UNKNOWN default, explicit Application Service checks, and a bounded Ollama service probe; registration, model readiness, hardware feasibility, resource capacity, generation, and routing remain distinct.

items.title: Model Resource Awareness
items.summary: Added bounded immutable model resource assessments from configured global/provider/model admission slots and provider registration, including the existing historical allocation-ID budget; snapshots reserve nothing and keep hardware feasibility and provider health unknown.

items.title: Controlled Concurrency
items.summary: Added an explicitly configured local controlled-execution path using existing Orchestrator routing and global/provider/model slot budgets, with duplicate-Task admission protection, nonblocking capacity rejection, and finally cleanup on success or failure; direct execution remains unchanged.

items.title: Execution Queue
items.summary: Added a durable Corporation-scoped FIFO execution queue with atomic explicit claims, immutable lifecycle snapshots, persisted Task-outcome acknowledgement, and confirmed human resolution; interrupted claims are never automatically replayed.

items.title: Resource Manager
items.summary: Added explicitly configured local execution-slot accounting with immutable global/provider/model capacity snapshots, atomic allocation/release, exhausted-capacity rejection, and unknown hardware/health reporting; existing execution paths remain unchanged.

items.title: Improved Task Planning
items.summary: Added immutable review-only Task plans for explicitly selected Tasks in one Project, with validated dependency graphs and deterministic order, actual lifecycle snapshots, authorized traced context, and caller-defined outcome/evidence criteria that remain unverified.

items.title: Context Retrieval
items.summary: Added bounded deterministic Context Retrieval over explicitly selected authorized memory scopes, with source references, provenance, expiry and revision traces, live scoped access rechecks, and explicit candidate/result/byte limit indicators.

items.title: Memory Management UI
items.summary: Added authorized memory inspection, owner correction and explicit retention, revision-conflict protection, expired-record removal, and owner withdrawal of immutable published knowledge through scoped API services and a browser page; default authentication remains fail-closed.

items.title: Corporation Knowledge
items.summary: Added explicit owner-approved Corporation Knowledge publication to bounded named-reader lists, with copied provenance and inherited expiry, deny-by-default scoped reads, owner revocation/withdrawal, and atomic durable publication; private memory is never shared automatically.

items.title: Project Knowledge
items.summary: Added private owner-scoped durable Project Knowledge with explicit Task provenance and verified project associations; reused retention/access rules and added non-destructive Task project-ID persistence without inferring historical links.

items.title: Persistent Conversation Memory
items.summary: Added explicitly opted-in SQLite conversation memory with immutable bounded records, owner/conversation-scoped retrieval, expiry enforcement, explicit deletion and scoped cleanup, and corrupt-data rejection; chat messages are never saved automatically.

items.title: Memory Architecture
items.summary: Defined immutable scoped memory records with explicit owners, note/summary types, required provenance and expiry, retention opt-in, and exact owner/scope retrieval checks without automatic sharing or storage.

items.title: AI Activity Visualization
items.summary: Added permission-aware Task lifecycle progress to the Activity page using protected Task detail reads, with explicit pending/running/completed/failed states, separate access errors, stale-response rejection, and no fabricated provider telemetry.

items.title: Corporation Task Creation via Chat
items.summary: Added immutable chat-to-Task reviews of completed user messages with explicit project and Agent routing; human CONFIRM creates a pending persisted Task without execution, and consumed reviews cannot be replayed.

items.title: Corporation Chat
items.summary: Added local Corporation Chat CLI commands with explicit coordinator Agent identity, Orchestrator-mediated replies, bounded prompts, isolated conversation history, and recorded response failures; no automatic Task creation or Web/API chat.

items.title: Chat Context
items.summary: Added caller-supplied context bounded to 8192 UTF-8 bytes per conversation, with atomic replacement, isolation, and clearing on successful closure; no retrieval, persistence, provider calls, or chat API/UI.

items.title: Individual Employee Chat
items.summary: Added in-memory conversations with explicit Employee/Agent scope, fixed target identities, and recorded message lifecycle without provider, persistence, or Task-execution integration.

items.title: Conversation Foundation
items.summary: Added in-memory Conversation and Message records with controlled message lifecycle and no provider, persistence, or Task-execution integration.

items.title: Corporation Updates page
items.summary: Added a protected, read-only Updates / Changelog page backed by a manually curated update manifest.
